title: Jobs without records; no royalties, reclaiming songs from MCA
summary: In those days a record was not needed to get work; she was never paid royalties or session fees and hopes to get songs back under the new copyright law.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But it would have been -- records, of course, helped, right?
And it helped that you had a record.
Yes, it did. But you see, you didn't have to have a record in those days in order to get a job.
Yeah, you have to have a record now, that's really selling, in order to get work. But I was lucky enough to always go from one job to another without a record.
I remember you once telling me that you -- well, you never got royalties, I know that.
But you didn't even get paid for the session.

No. And not only not paid for the session but I mean, they're still stealing from me. But you know, they have those contracts out now, those -- I got -- I want you to go over to my house and see it, where they have those things where even though you have signed contracts before, you can bring
You can bring them back to you. Bring
your songs back to you. That's good, because I'm going to get some of them back from MCA.

That's right. Because Mr. -- you know, Lovie needed money once, and she kept asking me to get money. And she told me, whatever you do with the songs, you do it. And I would try to get a little change for her to send to her, you know. And I think they took advantage of me on one of my songs, you know.
